raw_response.text: Natural language call routing can be treated as an instance of topic categorization of documents after speech recognition of calls. This categorization consists of two important parts. The first one is text preprocessing for numerical data extraction and the second one is classification with machine learning methods. In this paper, we investigate various text categorization methods for natural language call routing. The text preprocessing part includes tokenization, stop words removal, stemming and lemmatization, and numerical data extraction. For the classification part, we compare multiple machine learning methods including Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Random Forest. Experimental results show that the combination of these techniques can achieve high accuracy in natural language call routing.

raw_response.text: Insightful findings in political science often require researchers to analyze documents of a certain subject or type, yet these documents are usually contained in large corpora that do not distinguish between pertinent and non-pertinent documents. In contrast, we can find subsets of these larger corpora that are more focused on specific topics, which are termed as domain-specific corpora. However, it is not always feasible to have labeled data from domain-specific corpora, especially when dealing with sensitive information such as political documents. This paper presents an unsupervised domain adaptation approach, named Adaptive Ensembling (ADEN), for political document analysis. ADEN leverages a set of pre-trained classifiers across multiple source domains to form an ensemble model, and then fine-tunes the ensemble model on target domain data without requiring any labeled data. Experimental results on political document datasets demonstrate that our proposed ADEN outperforms existing methods by a significant margin.

raw_response.text: A regioselective synthesis of new mono and bisoxindoles containing bis spiro heterocyclic hybrids has been envisaged via 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition of azomethine ylides with the corresponding substituted ethyl acrylates using DBU as the base. The isolated yield of mono and bis oxindole derivatives was 60-85%. Among the synthesized compounds, 2,3-bis(4-methoxyphenyl)spiro[oxindole-3,1'-cyclohexane]-1,1'-diol (14) showed significant anti-proliferative activity against human colorectal adenocarcinoma (HCT-116) cell line with an IC50 value of 7.3 μM. Furthermore, compound 14 displayed remarkable antifungal activity against *Candida albicans* with an MIC value of 240 μg/mL. The molecular docking studies revealed that the interactions between the synthesized compounds and the target receptors were mainly hydrogen bonding and π–π stacking interactions. These results suggest that the synthetic bisoxindoles could be used as a scaffold for the design and development of new bioactive molecules.

Purpose – The purpose of this study is to explore the causal link between procurement route and ongoing buyer-supplier relationship.

Design/methodology/approach – The research draws on literature in the areas of: facilities management (FM) outsourcing; purchasing and supply chain management. Data were collected from 147 organizations operating in the FM sector via an online questionnaire. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was used to analyze the data. Findings – The study reveals that vertical integration has a negative impact on trust and information sharing whereas horizontal integration positively influences both trust and information sharing. Additionally, the findings indicate that trust and information sharing positively affect relational coordination. Originality/value – This study contributes to the body of knowledge in procurement routes and their impact on buyer-supplier relationships within the FM sector.

raw_response.text: Abstract: The widespread availability of many emerging services enabled by the Internet of Things (IoT) paradigm passes through the capability to provide long-range connectivity to a massive number of things, overcoming the well-known issues of ad-hoc, short-range networks. This paper investigates the support of massive machine-to-machine (M2M) traffic in heterogeneous networks (HetNets) and fifth-generation cellular networks (5G). Specifically, we explore the potential of HetNets and 5G to address the challenges posed by the massive scale and the variety of M2M traffic. We present a comprehensive analysis of the key enabling technologies for supporting massive M2M traffic in HetNets and 5G, including small cells, relay nodes, and advanced multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) techniques. Furthermore, we propose a new framework for optimizing the resource allocation and scheduling in heterogeneous networks to efficiently handle the massive M2M traffic. Simulation results show that our proposed framework can significantly improve the network performance in terms of throughput and delay compared to traditional approaches. The findings of this study provide important insights for future design and deployment of 5G and HetNet systems to support massive M2M traffic.

raw_response.text: Effects of a carboxylated styrene-butadiene-based liquid additive on the microstructure, mechanical strength and decolorization resistance of inorganic pigment layer in the color block have been examined. More dense inorganic pigment layer characterized by lower porosity and higher surface roughness was formed after incorporating the liquid additive into the inorganic pigment layer. The introduction of this additive significantly improved the interfacial adhesion between the inorganic pigment layer and the substrate, thereby enhancing the mechanical strength of the color block. Moreover, the decolorization resistance of the inorganic pigment layer was enhanced due to the increased interfacial adhesion and reduced porosity, which reduced the accessibility of chemicals to the inorganic pigment layer.

raw_response.text: In this work, we mainly investigate the effect of PT-symmetric operations on the dynamic behavior of the relative entropy of coherence for a two-level system within non-Markovian environments and put forward a feasible physical scheme to recover coherence by utilizing optimal parameters of PT-symmetry. The relative entropy of coherence (REoC) is a quantifier of coherence that captures the distinguishability between a given state and its incoherent counterpart. PT-symmetry, an extension of the standard Hermitian symmetry, allows for non-Hermitian Hamiltonians to exhibit real eigenvalues under certain conditions, which can induce novel physical phenomena. In quantum systems, non-Markovian environments introduce memory effects that can significantly affect the dynamics of coherence. Here, we explore how PT-symmetric operations can influence the coherence dynamics under non-Markovian environments and propose a method to optimize the parameters of PT-symmetry to enhance the recovery of coherence.

Endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-associated degradation (ERAD) is a principal mechanism that targets ER-associated proteins for cytosolic proteasomal degradation. Here, our data demonstrate a critical role for the Sel1L-Hrd1 complex in managing a key checkpoint during B cell development. The Sel1L-Hrd1 complex, an ERAD-I subunit, functions as a regulator of the B2 cell fate decision. Specifically, we found that loss of Sel1L or Hrd1 results in defective pro-B to pre-B cell transition, leading to reduced B cell development. Furthermore, we revealed that this process is mediated through the regulation of Mcl1 stability and subsequent activation of p53 signaling. Our findings elucidate the importance of the Sel1L-Hrd1 complex in managing a crucial regulatory checkpoint during B cell development, providing new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying B cell development.
